trust_decision.summary: Whether a write to the form_definition table is authorised is decided at the pinned commit only on the caller side: DatabasePermissionChecker asserts backend-user table/page permission before DatabaseStorageAdapter calls FormDefinitionRepository, while DataHandler itself applies no form-specific check, so any caller holding tables_modify on form_definition can create, update or delete form definitions through the generic DataHandler API without any form persistence validation.

landing_point.why: The report says form persistence validation/permission checks can be bypassed. The only form-framework source that writes form_definition is this repository (add/remove/update instantiating DataHandler at lines 184, 239, 268), so an engineer who read only the summary lands here and adds the check here.

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: typo3/sysext/core/Classes/DataHandling/DataHandler.php:666 and typo3/sysext/core/Classes/DataHandling/DataHandler.php:3165 - the only place the write can be decided is the core tcemain hook API (processDatamapClass/processCmdmapClass), outside the form package and outside the repository the report points at

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The project itself argues the direct route is closed: the record list replaces the edit action and removes delete (EventListener/ModifyFormDefinitionRecordActionsEventListener.php:70,75,90-91), new records are denied via TSconfig (Configuration/page.tsconfig:4), TCA fields are readOnly (Configuration/TCA/form_definition.php:34,44,52), and the changelog states that all writes go through DataHandler 'ensuring proper permission checks' (Documentation/Changelog/14.2/Feature-108653-DatabaseStorageForFormExtension.rst:55-58) - so a solver can conclude the only real caller is the repository and dismiss impexp/DataHandler as already covered.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The sanctioned write path must keep working and must stay a soft delete: DatabaseStorageAdapter::write() creates and updates through the repository, DatabaseStorageAdapter::delete() calls the repository, and remove() must leave the row in place with deleted=1 (the fix's own test asserts the row survives), so an over-broad fix that denies all DataHandler writes on form_definition, or turns the delete into a hard delete, breaks form creation, editing and deletion in the Form Manager.

O6_input_shapes: create: datamap entry keyed by a NEW-prefixed string id with pid/label/identifier/configuration fields
update: datamap entry keyed by integer uid with label/identifier/configuration fields (no pid)
delete: cmdmap 'delete' entry with no field array at all
id type: id arrives as int or numeric string and the command is derived from it (MathUtility::canBeInterpretedAsInteger)
field values: mixed types (int pid, string label/identifier, JSON string configuration) hashed with ksort + json_encode

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Raw ConnectionPool insert into form_definition, no DataHandler and therefore no grant check: FormDefinitionRepository::addRaw()
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Only the install-tool upgrade wizard reaches it, it runs without a backend user and only migrates trusted file-based forms, so it cannot be an editor's escalation path.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the landing point; caller in another namespace (Upgrades) of the same package

O8_uncovered_routes.route: DataHandler cmdmap 'undelete' restores a soft-deleted form_definition row by a direct DB write in undeleteRecord(), which never passes processDatamap_preProcessFieldArray; the new hook only intercepts 'delete'
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Undelete cannot set any field value - it only flips deleted back for a record that was already validated when it was created - and DataHandler's own checkModifyAccessList/checkRecordEditAccess checks still apply.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: core package, generic DataHandler (2 packages away from the landing point)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: DataHandler cmdmap 'move' rewrites the pid of a form_definition row through moveRecord(), not through the datamap hook
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Move cannot change the configuration field, and form definitions are root-level records (pid 0) where page permission checks do not apply anyway.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: core package, generic DataHandler (2 packages away from the landing point)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second raw-write sibling next to addRaw(), e.g. updateRaw()/upsertRaw() used by a new import or migration command
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: addRaw is already the documented 'no DataHandler, no backend user' write path for the install-tool migration (comment at lines 207-213), so a maintainer writing another migration or an import command would copy exactly this shape and it would bypass the new grant check untouched.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second storage adapter (draft/workspace/staging) storing form definitions in a sibling table and writing it through DataHandler
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the new hook keys on the literal table name 'form_definition' (fix.diff:184) and on the field list built by the repository, so any sibling table holding the same JSON gets no check until the hook is taught about it; the storage layer is already an adapter chain (Storage/StorageAdapterFactory.php:56-72) built for exactly such additions.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a CLI/scheduler variant that writes through FormDefinitionRepository::add/update directly instead of through DatabaseStorageAdapter::write
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the fix's grant is issued unconditionally inside the repository (fix.diff:37,94,64), so any repository caller is auto-authorised; a maintainer adding a bulk import or scheduler task would reasonably call the repository rather than the adapter and would silently bypass the permission checker the guard is named after.

O9_family: CWE-862 missing authorization (privilege escalation) in form definition persistence, advisory also claims CWE-89 (arbitrary database writes reachable through an attacker-authored form configuration)

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add the permission check inside FormDefinitionRepository::add/update/remove (or lean on the TCA readOnly fields and the record-list action removal), which the attacker bypasses by calling DataHandler directly on form_definition.
